title: THE COURTSHIP OF THE SILVER-CLASS GUARDIAN
about: Two Silver-class Rangers court each other by Socratic argument over a communal pickup truck: the opening question, the function, the circling debate, and the vow that the truck, and their desire, belongs to the State.

beats.text: Sunrise over the suburbs, the golden tower of Austin far off. A Silver-class Ranger stands by a pickup truck that the law says is shared property.
Across the lot, another Ranger polishes its side mirror. Among the Silver-class, courtship begins as an argument.
see: a woman polishing a car mirror

beats.text: Tell me, Ranger… what is an F-150?
A tool.
And is a tool good… because it is a tool— or because it performs its function well?
It sounds like conversation. It is really a way to settle who ranks higher, without saying so.
see: two people talking beside a truck

beats.text: It is good because it performs its function well.
Then define its function.
Its function is to carry. To tow. To endure. To be ready.
Ready for what?
For anything.

beats.ask: that's how he courted me, he argued with me

beats.text: A worker pushing a cart glances at them and keeps walking. The Ranger takes out a gauge and measures the truck's clearance, as if measuring its worth.
see: a man measuring a truck tire

beats.text: If you insist on measuring, let us measure correctly.
Define "correctly."
According to the Form of the Good.
Is "ready for anything" courage… or merely paranoia?
Is paranoia irrational… or simply prudence with a hat?
Is prudence a virtue…
—or a justification?

beats.ask: those two were made for each other

beats.text: They circle the truck as they argue. It is not a fight. They are falling into step, learning to move as one.
see: two horses running side by side

beats.text: Tell me, Daisy Thumos Jane: Does this truck belong to you?
No.
Does it belong to me?
No.
Then to whom does it belong?
To the State.
That is their vow: even what they want belongs to everyone. She hands him the shared key, and he takes it in both hands. A Ranger with a ruler steps them back to center.
see: a hand passing a set of keys
a man with a measuring stick

beats.text: They drive toward the golden tower. For one frame, the sky flickers. Here even love must be justified, preferably in writing.
see: a pickup truck driving down a highway
